answer: Atlas Path Divergence requires each agent to submit routes through three independently operated relay sets; admission needs disjoint paths across distinct operators. A willow class of relays must appear in at most a fixed fraction of any agent's recent paths. Karst monitors path overlap continuously. New identities must build non-repeating routing history over time, so mass registration yields correlated paths that fail divergence checks, forcing attackers to rent and rotate many operator-distinct relays, raising per-identity cost.
